newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Warner-Lambert to close Venezuela plant.
newsitem.headline: Warner-Lambert to close Venezuela plant.

text.p: Warner Lambert Co said Monday it planned to close its confectioneries plant in Venezuela as part of an international organization re-organization.

Warner, which produces the Adams brand chewing gums such as Chiclets, will concentrate its Latin American operations in Mexico, Colombia and Brazil, said Carlos Quintana, human resources director for Warner in Caracas.
"In Latin America Warner Lambert is concentrating on three plants in Cali, Colombia, Sao Paulo, Brazil and Puebla, Mexico," Quintana told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Plants in Peru, Ecuador and Guatemala have already been closed and operations in Argentina cut back by 90 percent, he said.
About 250 people are currently employed at the Caracas factory which should be shut down by the end of the year.
Warner Lambert have been operating in Venezuela since the 1950s and its existing plant was built in 1968.
Its pharmaceuticals division which markets the Parke-Davis brand drugs in Venezuela would remain in the country, Quintana said.
Its Adams brand chewing gums dominate the local market with more than 70 percent of market share and recorded total sales of about $25 million last year.
